lines: `timeout … agy --sandbox --mode plan … -p … < /dev/null` pattern, its mandatory closed stdin, its flag order and the
&& (cd "$(mktemp -d)" && timeout 600 agy --sandbox --mode plan $AGY_MODEL -p "<prompt>" < /dev/null)
input (`cat file | agy --sandbox --mode plan --model <slug> -p "…"`) is safe (the pipe EOFs). Always wrap in shell `timeout`. Same
re-testing the broken command. Correct: `agy --sandbox --mode plan [--print-timeout 15m] --model <slug> -p "…"`.
- **SANDBOX RULE (mandatory for analyst/read-only delegation, #157, #366):** every call that
should only READ is Pattern 1: `--sandbox --mode plan` from an empty cwd, content inline or piped,
no `--add-dir`. Un-sandboxed, agy has write/shell/git tools and an "analyst" can author and
git-commit code (S052 rogue auto-commit incident). Measured 2026-11-01 on 1.4.12: `--sandbox`
restricts only the shell, so native writes and reads work under it; `--mode plan` removes native
writes and the shell; the cwd is the workspace, so a call from a repo can read that repo. Open the
prompt with "Advisory only — do not modify any files; answer on stdout". The table and its limits
are in the `antigravity-cli` skill.
- **PATTERN 2 (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) has no containment:** full shell and git, reads home
and repos. Throwaway directory only, never a live repo as cwd or `--add-dir`; afterwards run
`git status --short` and compare `git log -1 --oneline` with the start, since status cannot see a
commit.

- For long-running prompts raise the wait timeout: `agy --sandbox --mode plan --model <slug> --print-timeout 15m -p "<prompt>" < /dev/null` (default `5m0s`). Keep `< /dev/null` even here — `--print-timeout` only guards the print phase, NOT the stdin read, so omitting it still hangs to the shell `timeout` (#135).

(cd "$PROJECT_DIR" && git ls-files -z '*.py' | xargs -0 tail -n +1) \
| (cd "$AGY_WORK" && timeout 600 agy --sandbox --mode plan $AGY_MODEL -p "Review the files on stdin for security issues" > review.txt) &

changes.old: - **FLASH-ONLY HARD-RULE (user directive 2026-07-24): agy runs gemini flash models ONLY — now enforced in code as well as stated.** `seat_model` accepts only `^gemini-\d+(\.\d+)*-flash-(high|medium|low)$` on every agy path (roster, freeze pin, env, harness literal). ✅ Listed on 2026-09-14 (`~/.claude/state/agy-models.json`, agy 1.2.2): `gemini-3.8-flash-{high,medium,low}` (newest), `gemini-3.7-flash-*`, `gemini-3.6-flash-*`. `gemini-3.5-flash-*` is no longer listed. ❌ FORBIDDEN with no carve-out, although agy lists them: `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-6-thinking`, `gpt-oss-120b-medium`, **and `gemini-3.1-pro-{high,low}`**. Reasons: (1) **provider diversity**, unchanged and fully binding — agy holds the third-model slot because it is neither Anthropic nor OpenAI; repointing it at `claude-sonnet-4-6` (the tempting "fix" for an agy no-show) collapses the cross-check into an echo, and `gpt-oss-*` collapses into the Codex arm; (2) **flash is Google's leading line**. This second reason has INVERTED. It used to read "flash-tier discipline — agy is advisory-tier, so don't reach for pro", which assumed pro > flash. That no longer holds: the pro line is stuck at `gemini-3.1-pro` while flash has reached 3.8, so `gemini-3.8-flash` is the smartest Google model on this account, and reaching for pro would buy an OLDER generation at higher latency. The rule stands; only its justification changed. On a no-show: retry under the STDIN/FLAG-ORDER/Pattern-2 rules, then record the provider gap honestly — there is no gemini fallback (retired 2026-07-25). Escalate to another arm rather than repointing agy.
changes.new: - **AGY FAMILY HARD-RULE (user directive; roster rev 6, 2026-10-21): agy serves ONE Gemini family, the one named by `model_roster.AGY_FAMILY` — enforced in code as well as stated.** Currently **Gemini 4 Argon**: `gemini-4-argon-{high,medium,low}` (listed 2026-10-20 in `~/.claude/state/agy-models.json`, agy 1.4.3). Reasons: (1) **provider diversity**, fully binding — agy holds the third-model slot because it is neither Anthropic nor OpenAI; repointing it at a `claude-*` model (the tempting "fix" for an agy no-show) collapses the cross-check into an echo, and `gpt-oss-*` collapses into the Codex arm; (2) **one family, the strongest Google line the account serves, chosen on evidence** — reaching for an older or different line buys nothing. Every agy call pins `--model` through `seat_model.py argv --role <role> --provider agy` (research and operational calls use `consultant_support`); the account default may still be flash, so an unpinned call rides a forbidden line. The one exception is measurement: the `model-eval-pack` skill may name any model agy lists, literally, only to measure it — never for a seat or delegated work. changes.old: - **MODEL RULE — pin it through `seat_model`; never ride the account default.** `agy` (current **1.2.2**) has a `--model` flag and an `agy models` subcommand; there is no short `-m` alias. `python3 ~/.claude/skills/_meta/seat_model.py argv --role <role> --provider agy` prints `--model <slug>`; place it before `-p` like every other flag. The resolver takes the newest listed flash version and the role supplies the level: `consultant_main` and `arbiter` get `-high`, `consultant_support` gets `-medium` (`gemini-3.8-flash-high` / `gemini-3.8-flash-medium` on the 2026-09-14 roster). A home-tier freeze in `~/.claude/state/seat-model-pins.json` can hold the version; `seat_model.py emit --json` shows what actually resolves. The account default appears to be **`gemini-3.6-flash`** (self-reported 2026-09-09, so indicative rather than verified), two generations behind 3.8: omitting `--model` silently seats a deliberation on an older line.
changes.new: - **MODEL RULE — pin it through `seat_model`; never ride the account default.** `agy` (current **1.4.3**) has a `--model` flag and an `agy models` subcommand; there is no short `-m` alias. `python3 ~/.claude/skills/_meta/seat_model.py argv --role <role> --provider agy` prints `--model <slug>`; place it before `-p` like every other flag. The resolver takes the newest listed version of the roster family (`model_roster.AGY_FAMILY`) and the role supplies the level: `consultant_main` and `arbiter` get `-high`, `consultant_support` gets `-medium` (`gemini-4-argon-high` / `gemini-4-argon-medium` on the 2026-10-20 roster); with `--size light|medium|complex` every role gets `-low` / `-medium` / `-high` instead (roster rev 7, `model_roster.AGY_LEVEL_BY_SIZE`). EVERY agy call pins it — deliberative seats `consultant_main`, research and operational calls `consultant_support`; the `model-eval-pack` skill alone passes `--model` literally, because choosing the model under test is its purpose. A home-tier freeze in `~/.claude/state/seat-model-pins.json` can hold the version; `seat_model.py emit --json` shows what actually resolves. The account default was self-reported as an older Gemini model (2026-09-09, indicative rather than verified) of a family the roster now forbids: omitting `--model` silently seats the call on a forbidden line.

re-testing the broken command. Correct: `agy --sandbox [--add-dir D] [--print-timeout 15m] --model <slug> -p "…"`.
- **SANDBOX RULE (mandatory for analyst/read-only delegation, #157):** `--sandbox` on every agy
call that should only READ — agy has write/shell/git tools by default, and an un-sandboxed
"analyst" can author and git-commit code (S052 rogue auto-commit incident). Scope caveat
(verified 2026-07-02, 1.0.15): `--sandbox` constrains shell/git commands only, NOT agy's
native file writes — do not `--add-dir` a writable live repo for consultancy (pipe content
instead), open the prompt with "Advisory only — do not modify any files; answer on stdout",
and run `git status --short` afterwards if a repo was exposed. Omit `--sandbox`
only when the task explicitly requires writes, and say so in the prompt.

- For long-running prompts raise the wait timeout: `agy --sandbox --model <slug> --print-timeout 15m -p "<prompt>" < /dev/null` (default `5m0s`). Keep `< /dev/null` even here — `--print-timeout` only guards the print phase, NOT the stdin read, so omitting it still hangs to the shell `timeout` (#135).
agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL -p "Review this code for security issues" < /dev/null

agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL --add-dir "$PROJECT_DIR" -p "Advisory only — do not modify any files; answer on stdout. Review for security issues in this project" < /dev/null
agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL -p "Use SCAMPER to generate ideas for reducing checkout abandonment. List each lens separately." < /dev/null
timeout 600 agy --sandbox $AGY_MODEL --add-dir "$PROJECT_DIR" -p "Review for security issues in this project" \
> "$AGY_WORK/review.txt" < /dev/null &
